"Forgive me, but I'm a bit busy preparing the refreshments. Please speak with my sister, Muriel. I'll be along shortly."

"Oh! You startled me! I was just organizing a few old papers, while awaiting your departure. Since it seems you will not leave, I suppose I shall return to the party and entertain my guests. I would ask that you follow me down, as I do not trust strangers wandering the upstairs halls without supervision."
"Be gone from my sight, you... you... adventurer! Go bother Muriel with your meddlesome questions. I'm busy!"
I'll leave when I'm good-and-ready.
I'll be along shortly, madam. Again, I'm sorry for if I've upset you.
<StartAction>[Spot] [What Alicine described as "old papers" looked very much like a journal.]</Start>
<StartAction>[Listen] [What Alicine described as "old papers" sounded very much like the thud of a thick, hardbound book.]</Start>
"Now, what...have...we...here? Seems there's an interloper in our midst, m'dear."

"You desire scraps from the master's table, dog? No...we don't share with feckless curs. We kill them. Now, I just have to decide how to do it. Shall it be acid this time or poison? Both sound so delectable; I simply can't decide."
"And leave you to summon the authorities, while our backs are turned. No, I think not. However, I'm undecided whether to use acid or poison? Both sound so delectable; I simply can't decide."
"Leave?! But we can't leave, while there's still fun to be had. Shall I douse <him/her> with acid, my sweet, or sting <him/her> with poison? Both sound so delectable; I simply can't decide."
"Oh, poison, my sadistic sugar-plum. Let it be poison. Just be sure and leave me a bit of fun, as well, this time."
"As you wish, honey-bun. I'll let you flay the skin from their bones. I know how the screams can get you so...well...worked up."
Correction. I'm an interloper who wants a cut of whatever you've pinched from this place.
Why you are sneaking about this wealthy home is really none of my business. Carry on.
It appears you two are robbing this home. I must ask you to vacate the premises at once!
Yes, I suppose a full cut of the takings would be more to my liking.
Well, I guess we're going to have to do this the hard way.
They'll be no flaying today, you villains!
"Tidings, citizen. You stand in the presence of Beb-Shuur, Master Theorosopher!"
"It is a title earned by years of painstaking study and devotion to the cause of our order."
"Obviously, this so-called brain of yours lacks the mental capacity to process complex subjects. Be gone from my sight! I have no desire to coddle imbeciles and dullards!"
"Explain to me the science of love, my friend, or art? Truth and beauty...are they not one and the same? As Master Vugu would so often say, 'Intuition trumps empiricism!'"

"It can't. That's the beauty of theorosophy. Your first instinctual cognition is always the right one. You simply use deductive reasoning to prove this hypothesis. As Master Vugu would say, 'Intuition trumps empiricism!'"
"Master Vugu, you see, was the first of us...our progenitor...the first 'Wise Man Atop the Cliff.' But he is lost to us now...so, I have taken up his mantle as leader of our order."
"Don't listen to this nonsense. I am the anointed 'Wise Man Atop the Cliff,' as chosen by Master Vugu himself."
"Oh, really...and just when did this succession ceremony take place, pray tell? On Vugu's deathbed?"
"Do not speak of the Master so! Vugu was the greatest mind of our age...a true visionary!"

"That is the subject of some debate between Xianga and I. You see, when our master leapt from these cliffs to his death, he believed his physical shell was an anchor against his spirit's desire to take flight."

"Vugu would often visit these cliffs to feed the gulls who congregate here. We believe he viewed birds as a living metaphor for our soul's desire to take wing, a theory our master was willing to put to the test."
"He left us..."
"Oh no, dear child. A theorosopher is nothing like a philosopher. A philosopher theorizes based on logic and empiricism, whereas we theorosophers rely entirely on deductive reasoning and intuition."
"The Master was filled with despair...and leapt from these cliffs to his death. A child standing nearby claims his last words were, 'Theorosophy is for the birds.'"
"We now know he was speaking in metaphors. Master loved feeding the gulls that congregate on these cliffs. We believe his study of these birds led him to some deeper meaning."

"Yes, we believe it has something to do with how the birds ride the winds... We believe our master hoped his own belief system would help him ride aloft the winds and take flight...metaphorically and otherwise."

"If successful, it would prove once and for all that intuition trumps empiricism, thus establishing theorosophy as a cornerstone of future studies in rhetorical theory. Very soon, I shall follow the Master's example and take the plunge."
"Charlatan! Mountebank! It is I, Xianga, who shall follow our master's example and leap from the sacred cliffs!"
"Hmm... Interesting. So, the survivor would attain the mantle as new leader of the Order. A wise proposition."
"Yes, a capital idea. Let us put our theorosophizing to the test!"
"Spoken like a true empiricist. Be gone from my sight!"
"With scorn fueled by envy. These so-called 'scientists' hide behind tomes of empirical data. They cannot break free from years of theoretical indoctrination. They are to be pitied."
"Master Vugu's journal?! What a find this is! Please, let me see it!"
"We theorosophers use our deductive skills to validate naturally held principles."
"No. My intuition tells me this is not the writings of my former master, Vugu of Cormyr. He would never write such things in this journal. This work is slanderous and a complete forgery."

"That signifies nothing. The tenets of Theorosophy proclaim that one's gut reaction to a situation is always the correct response. Since my fellow theorosopher proclaims the journal to be false, it must be so."

"Yes, and I can prove it. In all the years I knew Master Vugu, he never once spoke of keeping a journal. This wretched tome is an obvious attempt by one of his envious rivals to slander the Master's good name."

"Yes, I concur. Vugu's theories were often the subject of intense deliberation within the philosophical community. It does not surprise me that some would attempt to tarnish the memory of the great Master Vugu!"

"It is guilt that drives them towards lashing out at theorosophy and those who preach it. Deep down they know we speak the truth. They know that deductive reasoning is meant to bolster a being's innate precognition."

"The proof of the gut, my friend...the science of the soul! Intuition is our subconscious rising up from deep within our psyche to guide our steps and proffer us answers! We use deductive reasoning to uphold our innate precognition."
"Oh, you again. Is there something you need of the future Master Theorosopher?"
"I told you to leave me be! Now go!"
"It would to someone unskilled in modern, rhetorical theory. You see, we theorosophers use our deductive skills to validate naturally held principles."
"Indeed. Take, for example, the encampment to our north. One sees a brightly-colored tent with youthful men and women performing drills and calisthenics. It is, quite obviously, a traveling circus."

"Precisely. Take, for example, the encampment to our north. One sees a brightly-colored tent with youthful men and women performing drills and calisthenics. It is, quite obviously, a traveling circus."
"Since my gut reaction was to look upon the scene and proclaim, 'that is a traveling circus,' my next step involves simply proving it is so via deductive reasoning."

"Well...perhaps so, but that's beside the point. You see, my gut reaction is to look upon the scene and proclaim, 'that is a traveling circus.' My next step involves proving it is so via deductive reasoning."

"Yes. My initial assumption is 'traveling circus,' so I use deductive reasoning to support this theory, since theorosophers believe intuition is the key to understanding the true nature of the multiverse."
Well then, I'll leave you to your...theorosophizing.
That's an important sounding title you have.
A traveling circus?!
You're speaking complete nonsense. I must leave before my brain turns to mush.
Yes, we should part ways before I part your skull...
Though I suspect it is not my mental capacity that is the problem here, I will leave you be.
Very well. I shall leave you to your studies.
What about science?
What if your deductive reasoning leads you to make a different assumption?
So, who is the new Master of Theorosophy?
What happened to your master?
Theorosopher? Is that anything like a philosopher?
I think you both should jump.
<StartAction>[The two men leap from the cliff, thus ending the Order of Theorosophers before it even began.]</Start>
My advice to you both is to think before you jump.
Yes, we should part ways before I part your skull...
Good luck with your theorosophizing... You're gonna need it.
Very well. I shall leave you to your studies.
I'll leave you two to your discussions.
How were Master Vugu's theories viewed by other philosophers?
Hmm...intriguing. Tell me more.
Actually, I think you and your friend are the piteous ones in this situation.
Theorosophy, you say? I think I have a journal here from your late master you might be interested in.
<StartAction>[You wait as Beb-Shuur quickly thumbs through the journal.]</Start>
But I found the journal in a cave nearby, the one most likely occupied by your former master.
But you and the fellow next to you are both named in the journal.
A forgery? What proof do you have?
Just wanted to see how your theorosophizing was coming along. Good day.
Deductive reasoning AND intuition? Sounds counterintuitive to me.
Sounds logical enough.
You use deductive reasoning to enforce your pre-existing beliefs?
Your deductive skills are truly amazing.
Looks like a castle siege to me.
"Ahoy there, landlubber! What brings ya to Daggerford?" This old salt has a knavish twinkle in his eye.
"Fair enough. I can understand the need for secrecy in these troubled times. Good luck to ya!"
"Well, that's a little complicated, friend."

"Ya see, mine was a very normal childhood. I was raised in a nice home with plenty to eat and clean clothes on me back. But then, I put out to sea...and..." Bill pauses, wistfully recalling days of yore.

"Well, if you be in such a hurry, I'll just get back to sippin' my pint o' grog and wish you happy trails. Just don't come back expectin' Bill to spill 'is guts. Once you tell ol' Bill to shut 'is trap, it stays shut!"
"Well, the story begins with me maiden voyage. I was a merchant seaman then, a card-carryin' member of the Mariners' Alliance."
"Understandable. Only so much time in the day, after all. Good luck to ya!"
"Sorry, friend. I get a bit misty-eyed when I think back on me maiden voyage. I was a merchant seaman then, a card-carryin' member of the Mariners' Alliance."
"Well, from when I was a wee lad, growin' up on the back streets o' Waterdeep, I always felt sort o' drawn to the sea."
"There was this constant pullin' at me heartstrings, like some harpy callin' me to her dread bosom."
"But she is, my friend, and I've never met a more fickle lover in all my years. One second she's callin' ya to her with the voice of a diva. The next she's dashin' yer ship to pieces on the rocks."
"It was like that my first night at sea. Without a drop o' rain in sight, nor wind to fill our sails, the ship starts heavin' to and fro like we're caught in a gale."
"Aye, you can smell it on the wind, <lad/lass>. When you been out at sea as long as I have, you get a feelin' for these kinds of things..."

"They're a good bunch o' swabbies, if a bit shy and secretive 'round strangers. If ya ever want to cozy up to one of 'em, just feed 'em booze...lots and lots of booze. Those lads and lasses really love their Harbor Bottom Whiskey."
"Why the barkeep in this 'ere establishment sells some, though I wouldn't wish the stuff on me worst enemy... It gives a whole new meanin' to the phrase 'rot-gut whiskey.'"

"Aye, I was indeed. So I'm workin' for the Alliance and the first night at sea the ship starts heavin' back and forth like we're caught in a gale. Except there wasn't a drop o' rain in sight, nor wind to fill our sails."

"The captain had us strap ourselves to the masts while he tried to steer us to safety. But, just as he grabbed hold o' the wheel, we spied the cause o' the disturbance, as the kraken's first tentacle grabbed hold o' the main mast."
"Now, sailors and krakens have a long history of not gettin' along. So, when this one spied our captain pullin' hard at the wheel, it snatched 'im up in its mighty beak."
"Aye, he did indeed... Good man, the captain, who taught me everything I know about survivin' at sea...but we'd best get back to the story now, as the good part's fast approachin'!"
"Well, it뭩 a kind of oversized squid with a foul temper and a taste for sailors... Now, I best be gettin' back to the story, as we're comin' to the good part."

"I remembered me grandpa, who was quite the seaman himself, tellin' me how krakens ain't too fond o' fire, as they don't see it much at the bottom o' the sea. So I told a few of the lads to sling some lamp oil at the beast and torch the ballistas." Bill's eyes alight with a fiendish twinkle.

"The first bolt from the ballista lit the thing up like a candle! I can still hear its shrieks in me head. After that, the crew sort o' saw me as their new captain. They also decided that workin' for the Mariners' Alliance wasn't all it was krak'd up to be -- 'scuse the pun -- so we broke out on our own as 'freelancers.'"

"With me new occupation as lawless scoundrel, I needed a name change, so I added the 'Black' to the beginning. When I'm back in port, so as not to draw attention, I just resort back to Bill...just plain ol', law-abidin' Bill O'Shaughnessy."
"Just take care and watch your back. This storm will blow through soon enough, and when it does I suspect we'll have a few good folks go overboard, if you get my meanin'..."
"Me former captain was an honest sailor and look where it got 'im... No, I learned long ago that it's best to leave the honest part o' me in port, 'cause it just ain't fit for a battle with the sea."
"Tall tale nothin'! That there is the true-blue story of how William Henry O'Shaughnessy became the dread pirate, Black Bill, most feared cutthroat in all of Faerûn."
"Ha ha! Thank ya kindly, <sir/madam>. We two will do our best."

"Aye, pleasure to see you again, <lad/lass>. I'll be puttin' out to sea soon and advise you to do the same. Ill winds are blowin' through Daggerford these days." Bill exhales a heavy sigh laced with dread.
"A work-for-hire <lad/lass>, eh? Pleasure to meet you. Me name is Bill, though you'll hear some 'round here callin' me by my other name, 'Black Bill,' which is the one I use when I'm at sea."
"Me name is Bill when I'm dry-docked, or 'Black Bill' when I'm at sea."

"Aye, them's honest swabbies on shore leave. Me? Why, I been called many words in my time, <lad/lass>, but 'honest' ain't one of 'em!" A slightest hint of a smile forms at the corners of Bill's bearded mouth.
"Truth be told, ol' Bill's a bit of an enigma really."
"You mean like those other swabbies wanderin' around town on shore leave? Nawww! Those lads and lasses play by the rules. Whereas, I see the rules as somethin' meant to be broken."
"Plenty. Ya see, I used to be one o' them work-for-hire swabbies. I was a card-carryin' member o' the Mariners' Alliance."
I'm afraid that's none of your business, sir.
Stow it, ya old codger.
Are you a sailor?
What can you tell me about the other sailors?
Why the need for two names, Bill?
Tell your life story to someone else.
You won't see me again, old-timer. Of that you can be sure.
Fair enough. See you around, Bill.
On second thought, maybe I should listen to your tale after all.
I'm afraid I've little time for sea shanties, Bill.
And to you, sailor.
And to you, Bill.
Yes?
What made you want to become a sailor?
You talk of the sea like it's some living entity.
What was it like working for the Mariners' Alliance?
Sound advice, Bill. Now, if you'll excuse me, I really need to be moving on.
Where can I purchase some of this Harbor Bottom Whiskey?
Sound advice, Bill. Now I believe you were about to explain why you have one name in port and another at sea.
Troubled times?
Your captain died bravely, Bill.
What's a kraken?
Sounds terrible. What did you do?
So, you answer your former captain's bravery by turning to a life of piracy.
I've heard some tall tales in my time, Bill, but that one puts the rest to shame.
Well, thanks for the tale, Bill, and good luck with those dual personalities.
Thanks for the warning, Bill. Take care of yourself.
I do, Bill. Thanks for the warning.
I'm a mercenary and came in with one of the caravans.
Just passing through. Can I ask your name, sir?
You're not dressed like the other sailors in this place.
If you're not a sailor, then you must be a pirate.
"Yesss...a tiny morsel crawls across my plate... You smell of <CUSTOM501>...not my favorite, but it shall do in a pinch."
"You show deference to your betters, <CUSTOM501>. I am...touched. Very well. Speak to me your desires...before I blast them into ruin."
"Thieves all! They wished to take what was mine! I acted only in self-defense! Pleeeease, good <CUSTOM501>. I beg you to stay your hand!"
"You are all that and more, great one. Pleeease...let me live."
"You mean Peredus the Great? How comical. Were the man great, his bones would not lie as souvenirs within my hoard. But enough about him, let's discuss the real reason you've come...your escape."

"My kind has a certain fondness for gold. So, what better place to set up one's lair than within the caves that adjoin a well-used wishing well? But this talk of lairs and gold bores me. Let's get to the real reason why you're here...your desire to find a way out of these caverns."
"I have a cave nearby that leads to the surface. However, even if I allowed you to enter the passage, which of course I cannot, you'd find yourself walking into a veritable hornet's nest..."
"Because I must feast on your flesh and add your bones to my ever-growing stockpile. Now, get thee into my stomach where you belong!"

"Nothing to match my prowess, but there is a lizardfolk priest who has been stirring up trouble of late. It seems he has allied himself with a being of great power...a devil who desires vengeance of some sort or other. These devils seem to hop from one vendetta to the next. It's really quite amusing."
"Nothing that would interest you, <CUSTOM501>, as you'll be long dead before the devil moves upon its quarry. Now, I believe I was about to feast upon your succulent flesh."
"Ha ha ha... The <CUSTOM501> shows spirit, which is good. I find a dose of courage helps to tenderize the meat. Come, brave one! Get thee into my stomach where you belong!"
"Please... Do not slay me, oh mightiest of foes! I surrender to your will!"
<StartAction>[Bow down.]</Start> Oh great lord of earth and sky, hear my plea!
What do you know of the spirit who inhabits these caves?
Though I generally do not parley with dragons, I was wondering if you might know the way out of these caverns.
You have supped your last on <race> flesh, wyrm! Prepare to be cast into the Abyss!
<StartAction>[Attack.]</Start> Die, foul creature!!
Spare you? How many corpses fill your chambers, wyrm?
Bow to me, wyrm, and claim me as your new master!
Go, wyrmling, before I change my mind!
<StartAction>[Attack.]</Start> You are a vile wyrm, with a heart as black as night. Your death is the only true justice!
Why does a black dragon of such power and majesty dwell in these caverns?
I wish only to pass safely through your domain and return to the surface.
Why can you not allow me passage?
I'll take my chances...with you and with the perils that await me on the surface.
What perils lie on the other side, oh great one?
What do you know of this devil and its vendetta?
I think you'll find this meal a bit hard to chew.
"Yes...um...he-hello?" Though dressed for battle, this young woman's cracking voice and wide eyes tell you she's absolutely terrified.
"The-the-the...test, mi<lord/lady>. We're on the Kn-n-n-ight's T-t-t-trial."
"The M-m-m-mighty...R-r-r-rat...of C-c-c-cunning...D-d-d-demeanor." The poor lass seems newly terrified at the mere mention of the creature.
"D-d-d-d-don't s-s-s-sayyy its n-n-name al-l-l-loud. *Gulp*"
"It'll kill us all! *Sob*...rend our flesh! *Sob*"
"You're b-b-b-back! D-d-d-d-did you encounter the b-b-b-beast?"
"Did you k-k-k-kill it?!!"
"Eeeek!! It's the cunning rat!! It's followed <him/her> out! Run for it!!"
"'Tis the beast itself! The cunning rat of...but wait, friends...for it appears quite tame...sort of sad, in fact."
"Sad and...kind of cute... Say, maybe we could tell Lord Peneshay and the others that we not only conquered the rat but captured it?!! We'll be famous!"
"That's it?!"
"But he's just a little rat, like the kind I used to hit with a sling at my uncle's farm."
"We th-th-three are s-s-squires in the Order of T-t-t-tye."
"And to think I lost my lunch over that! I feel so...embarrassed!"
"Thank you, <sir/madam>, for saving our lives and our careers! We shall return to the Order of Tye as heroes, thanks to you! Three cheers for the mighty adventurer, lads!"
"Blessed day!! Good show!"
"Well done, <sir/madam>! Well done indeed!"
"I...I'm feeling a bit better now. Your bravery has lent me courage to face the danger inside this cave."
"You're right, of course. I...I am feeling a bit better now." Your words seem to have bolstered the young lady's courage.

"We are knights in training in the Order of Tye, which is an elite guard unit that resides in Waterdeep. Our main duty is to serve as royal escorts to members of the Lords' Alliance when they leave the city on one of their many excursions."
"The prestige associated with this post means the Order receives numerous applications. This caused Lord Peneshay to enact a rigorous initiation process that culls applicants down to a select few."
"Some applicants fall prey to dangerous training exercises that include live traps. Others, like us, are sent on suicide missions...to slay unbeatable foes like the one that lies within these caves."
"He's the current head of the Order of Tye. We feel honored to have progressed this far through his screening process."
"It's the way of the Order, <sir/madam>. We feel quite lucky to have progressed as far through the screening process as we did."
Do you mind telling me why three well-armed knights are quaking in their boots from fear?
Do you mind telling me why the three of you are standing in front of this cave?
Who is Lord Peneshay?
That doesn't sound exactly fair.
I've heard enough. If this beast is part of your Order's cruel initiation, so be it!
Perhaps it's time you told me what you face.
Tell me the nature of the beast inside, and I might be willing to slay it for you.
We'll see about that.
I'll take my chances, lad. Be back soon.
<StartAction>[Paladin or Fighter]</Start> Get ahold of yourself, soldier! A knight faces danger with a stout heart and a sturdy shield.
Not yet. Please try to calm yourselves in the meantime.
I did.
No... I chose a different approach.
Yup, and here's its skin as proof.
Calm yourself, madam, and tell me of this Order of Tye.
Hero worship...aahh...so very nice.
The lesson learned here, soldiers, is that fear is often your greatest enemy. Farewell and good luck.
Farewell to you, and work on being a bit more courageous in the future.
Please relax yourself, madam. I assure you that whatever you're up against will have to deal with me first.
You're the most pathetic knights I've ever seen. I will leave you three here to wallow in your cowardice.
Now, tell me why the three of you are out here.
"Talk to the boss."
I'll do that. Thanks.
"Help! I need help, please!!!" This poor child is emotionally distraught. Tears stream down her face in rivulets of unbidden agony.
"Well...I was fishing...with...with...live bait...and my doggie tried to...to... Oh, it's terrible, and it's all my fault!!!"
"Will you go save him for me?!! Tell me you will. Pretty pretty please!! He's my bestest friend in the whole wide world!"
"You can take the rope off the mooring, since you won't be out in the lake."
"You better hurry, <mister/missus>! I'll wait right here until you get back!"
"You will?! Yippeeeee!!! Just take my boat over to the island and look for a big, black hole."
"But I wasn't by myself, <mister/missus>. I had Fluffy! And he's the best...only he likes to eat worms...which is why he tried to jump up and bite my bait...which is why he fell down the hole."
"Oh, go away! I told you that Fluffy's hurt, but you won't help me! And now poor Fluffy's all alone...at the bottom of that big, dark hole!"
"Please go help, Fluffy! I'll wait right here, until you get back!"

"So, the big, kind adventurer comes to rescue the little girl's doggie who fell down the scary black hole... How sweet... It's almost enough to bring a tear to my eye...if I weren't laughing so hard."
"There. That's better... I was beginning to feel nauseous from playing the sugary-sweet waif who lost her poor, little doggie."
"Not entirely. I do have a potential pet from my hometown I'd like you to meet and maybe adopt, if it suits you. Say hello to Fluffy?"
"I...I'm sorry...<mister/missus>...can't talk...he's on the island...fell down a hole... Oh, Mommy!!!"
"From your reaction it appears you don't care for Fluffy very much. Maybe you'll like her brother, Moxxy, better. Here Moxxy! Here boy!"
"Hmm... So, you don't seem to like Moxxy much either, eh? Well, how about I just bring out the whole brood and you can pick which one you like."

"Now, I encourage you to play with the pets, before you make your choice. However, I would urge you to choose quickly, as their games tend to get a little...rough. Farewell and good luck my brave adventurer!"

"Oh, but that's not very nice. You know, all baatezu are not mean and cruel. In fact, some of us even keep pets. Maybe you'd like to see a few from my hometown. You might find one that suits you...like Fluffy here, for example."

"Hello again, my friend. Is there something you wish of me?" The young gnome studies you carefully, his large black eyes lingering a bit too long on your backpack.
"Skills? Why, all manner of skills, though most fall squarely within the realm of deception and trickery."
"My name is Purfbin Doogrick, and I'm newly arrived in Daggerford, by way of the Trade Way. My former home was Waterdeep."
"Some would call me a 'thief,' though I prefer the title "professional treasure hunter.' I seek rare artifacts and items of great power."
"Greetings, <FirstName>. Would you care to enjoy the pleasure of my company once again? Personally, I would welcome another opportunity to share in the profitable rewards of adventure."
"Yes? Is there something you need?"
"Are you sure?" Purfbin looks disappointed. "I would like very much to continue our adventures."
Purfbin nods approvingly. "Good idea."
"Fear not, fellow adventurer! I can find my own way home."
"Fine, but save some of the good loot for me too!"
"Yes? What do you want me to do?"
Text: "그래, 날 시켜서 뭘 하라고?"

TextEng: "Is there something else?"
"Of course." Purfbin eyes your pack closely and jokes, "If you should happen to die in an unfortunate accident, I shall take very good care of your possessions."
Text: "정말? 음... 그렇다면야..."

TextEng: "Mine is a lengthy, ponderous tale, and one which I've already related to countless occupants of this fine establishment. It seems sailors will proffer alcohol in exchange for a fine, ripping yarn."
Purfbin pats several of the many bulging pockets sewn into his robes. "I might have a few wires and gizmos in here to help with even the most stubborn of traps."
Text: "좋아, 최선을 다해볼게."

TextEng: "My Granda Retsotnert always used to say that running was the better part of bravery. And believe me, I've done my share of running!"
Text: "몰래 기어 다니긴 그만두고 이제 뛰라고? 알겠어."

TextEng: "I will try not to make even the smallest of sounds."
Text: "좋아! 은밀하게 가는 거지!"

TextEng: "Then what do you have me around for?" He shrugs. "Suit yourself."
Text: "그럼 날 데리고 다니는 이유가 뭐야?" 그는 어깨를 으쓱합니다. "좋을 대로 해."

TextEng: Purfbin pats several of the many bulging pockets sewn into his robes. "I might have a few wires and gizmos in here to help with even the most stubborn of locks." He smiles mischievously, "Of course, after I open a chest, I might be tempted to remove a few of the more valuable items!"
Text: "응, 그런 건 당연히 내 도움이 필요하지."

TextEng: "I was so hoping that you would mention that!" Purfbin jokes, "You haven't had a chance to bath recently, have you?"
Text: "그래서 얼마나 떨어져 있으라구?"

TextEng: "Yes! An excellent suggestion! I'm certain that the air will be much fresher upwind!"
"Yes! I can still keep an eye on your pack." Purfbin laughs, "Sorry, I meant to say back! I can still keep an eye on your back!"
"That wasn't what I had in mind, friend." Purfbin shrugs and winks, "but it does afford me the opportunity to borrow what I need from your pack!"
Text: 그는 어깨를 으쓱한다. "좋아, 뭐."

TextEng: "Excellent! That means I'll get first share of their loot, right?"
Text: "그냥 달려 들어가라고? 좋아!"

TextEng: "I'm afraid repeated tellings might result in the cessation of speech altogether. Ask me again, mi<lord/lady>, when my vocal chords have had some time to recover.
He nods. "I can do that."
Text: 그는 고개를 끄덕입니다. "최선을 다해볼게."

TextEng: "Fine, but don't take anything that doesn't belong to you."
Text: "좋아, 알았어. 근데 피투성이 손으로 막 더듬거리는 건 금지야."

TextEng: "You are inviting me to look through your pack? How very...trusting...of you." Purfbin quickly grabs your pack and starts rummaging around joking, "Do not worry, friend! I shall let you know if I find anything in here that I want!"
"You want to pilfer goods from my pack?" Purfbin jokes, "Go ahead. Help yourself. I have already hidden the best loot where you'll never find it...deep in my pockets!"
"Talk? But we seek the Great Prize...and talk will only slow us down... *sigh*. Very well, what do you wish to talk about?"

"I'd be feeling much better with a few more gold pieces in my pockets," Purfbin jokes, as he casually pats several of the bulging pockets on his colorful robes. "I don't suppose you care enough to make a small donation?"
Text: "다 완전 끝내줘. 더할 나위 없지. 뭐... 내가 엄청 부자에 글래머한 하플링 아가씨들 하렘에 둘러싸여 있으면 더 좋겠지만... 그건 당장은 안 되겠지, 하하하!"

TextEng: "Is there something else that you wish to discuss with me?"
Text: "다른 특별한 얘기 있어?"

TextEng: "We need less talking and more looting!" Purfbin winks as he rubs his small hands together with obvious glee.
Text: "가스가 좀..." 그의 눈이 휘둥그레지더니, 갑자기 요란하게 트림을 내뿜습니다. "아, 됐다. 신경 꺼."

TextEng: "I'm happier than a fat mole in a hole full of dirt!" Purfbin laughs heartily as he pats his over-stuffed pockets. "Except, this mole isn't collecting dirt, if you know what I mean!"
Text: "왜 나한테 신경을 써? 가서 할 일이나 해."

TextEng: "Well, <FirstName>, I was thinking...how do you feel about increasing my share of the loot? No? Oh do not be so hasty, my friend! We can talk about this later, perhaps when you're feeling more generous?"
Text: "알았어, 알았어. 그냥 머릿속으로 내 회고록을 쓰는 중이었거든."

TextEng: "Lost something?! No...no...not at all. It's a simple affectation, from years of carrying around valuable items in these bulbous pockets of mine."
"Wonderful! I just had the most amazing idea for a prank involving a crossbow and a decapitated orc's head. Would you like to...oh...never mind."
Text: "나쁘진 않아. 문명이 있는 곳으로 돌아가면 서커스에 들어가볼까 생각 중인데, 어때?"

TextEng: "Excellent!" Purfbin smiles gleefully as he pauses momentarily to sniff the air. "Can you smell that? It's the smell of opportunity! There's a very rich <man/woman> nearby who is not guarding <his/her> possessions closely enough." He winks at you.
Text: "피 묻은 전리품에서 내 몫 좀 더 챙겨줘도 좋고. 헤헷."

TextEng: "This is a fine <day/night> to be relieving unwary folks of their possessions. No...no...I wouldn't call it stealing, exactly. I mean, if a rich man can't be troubled to take care of his possessions, then he probably doesn't deserve 'em...that's what I always say!"
Text: "엉덩이에 종기가 하나 난 것 같긴 한데, 그거 말곤 완전 멀쩡해."

TextEng: "I might be blind, but do not despair, <FirstName>, for we gnomes are used to walking around in the dark!"
Text: "괜찮을 거야, 아마. 근데 여기가 정말 어두운 건지... 내가 진짜 눈이 먼 건지 말해 줄래? 살짝 걱정돼서."

TextEng: "I have a few small cuts and bruises, but we have more important matters to discuss right now." Purfbin smiles and jokes, "Matters such as how best to increase my share of the loot!"
Text: "프흣, 난 걱정 마. 그냥 긁힌 상처 몇 개야."

TextEng: "So much blood!" Purfbin looks down at the blood splattered on his robes and sighs. "I never liked the sight of blood. Especially when it's my own!"
Text: "아까 좀 엉망이 되긴 했지, 헤. 볼 것까지는 없어."

TextEng: "I am very badly injured, friend." Despite his grave wounds, Purfbin smiles and jests, "If you force me to walk another footstep, I may drop down dead at your feet."
Text: "그냥... 몇 군데 긁혔을 뿐이야, 별거 아냐." 그는 얼굴을 찡그리며 빈 팔로 배에서 솟는 심한 피를 틀어막으려 합니다.

TextEng: "I have been poisoned! My stomach feels like it is trying to crawl up my throat and visit my tongue! Oh...this is worse than that time when Ellywick spiced my breakfast cereal with Halruaan hot peppers!"
Text: "어이! 완전 멀쩡해-내 혈관을 타고 흐르는 불덩이만 빼면 말이지. 그건... 알아서 해결되겠지..."

TextEng: "Well, <FirstName>, my skin is covered with brown itchy spots." Purfbin laughs as he waves one of his diseased arms under your nose. "It is probably contagious, you know!"
Text: "피부에 이상한 반점이 좀 생긴 것만 빼면 나쁘지 않아. 이거... 안 좋은 건가?"

TextEng: "Well, <FirstName>, all gnomes come from very large families. Granda Retsotnert always used to say that there's no such thing as an empty burrow!"

"I prefer the title 'professional treasure hunter'... You see, I'm not one for common skulduggery, like slitting purses and lifting wallets. No, I'm more interested in the recovery of rare artifacts and items of great power."
"It was joyous...wondrous... Each day was a new adventure! While we gnome children played together in close quarters, the earth above our heads trembled with the sounds of our laughter!"
"Indeed! Let me relate to you a story of my own prankish behavior during a visit to Baldur's Gate."

"I...I would rather not discuss that with you, <FirstName>...not now...not yet..." Purfbin's head drops, shielding his eyes from you. "Instead, let me relate to you a story of my visit to Gond's High House of Wonder in Baldur's Gate."
"No! I don't want to talk about my family, <FirstName>. Would you like to hear my story about Baldur's Gate?"

"Located in the heart of the Great City, Gond's High House of Wonders is a grand museum which displays all of the great gnomish inventions, such as Gurn's Great Gnomeflinger and Baldric's Brilliant Blamblower."

"Gnomeflingers are truly amazing inventions! Gurn, an old, wizened gnome with unusually weak knees, invented the Gnomeflinger to help him ascend the great central staircase of Candlekeep. The Gnomeflinger employs a complex array of springs, gears, and cogs to rapidly catapult its wearer upwards at a great velocity."
"It was a sunny day in Baldur's Gate, around noon, and I was taking my leave of Duke Entar Silvershield's estate. I was crawling under the fence when one of his unpleasant-looking guards spotted me."
"My 'posterior' was sort of...well...stuck. I really do need to cut back on the ale and sausages... In fact, it was one particularly splendid meal that got me into this whole mess."

"While enjoying a meal at the Prancing Pony, I overheard a story about a certain rare and valuable gem which old Silvershield kept in his study. My purse was depressingly light that day, so I had sufficient motivation to investigate."

"After absconding with the gem, I left Silvershield's estate with his loyal guards hot on my heels. I sought refuge in Gond's High House of Wonder, but was spotted by the duke's guards who quickly surrounded the museum."
"Since the rarest trinkets are often in the possession of people in a similar line of work to my own, I often find myself thieving from other thieves."
"I was trapped! The duke's dour-faced guards had sealed off the exits, and were waving those sharp pointy sticks, while advancing towards my location."
"It was those large, unwieldy things that human guards are so fond of carrying around." Purfbin looks confused, and shrugs.

"As the guards closed in on my location in the Grand Gallery, I beheld a large glass skylight. Sunlight spilled down from the heavens like a blessing from the gods! Sweet freedom, but so far out of reach! The gallery's white-washed walls were too smooth to climb." Smiling, Purfbin taps his bulging paunch, "I'm not the most 'athletic' of gnomes, I'm afraid."
"We're almost to the punch line, <FirstName>!"

"Close to my hiding spot, I spied Gurn's Great Gnomeflinger on display! I quickly strapped myself in and cranked the handle. As the Gnomeflingers' gears ground, I heard the duke's guards crash through the front doors."

"Just before their hands were on me, I pushed the eject button, and shot up towards the heavens, crashing through the skylight. I landed with a heavy thud upon the hard slate roof!" Purfbin sheepishly points a finger at his waistline, "It seems my bones had more than enough padding to ensure a safe landing."

"My heart pounded with exhilaration, as glass from the broken skylight rained down on the stunned guards below, providing me just enough time to slide down a nearby drain pipe... Soon after, I celebrated my escape in the local pub."

"Well, I can assure you that every word is true. If you're ever in Baldur's Gate, just mention the name 'Purfbin,' and you're sure to get a chuckle or two. Now, is there anything else I can help you with, <FirstName>?"
"Oh, but that's different. We gnomes are naturally soft-footed, so keeping quiet is second nature. Then, it's just a matter of picking the odd lock and I'm in! But let's get back to the story..."
"Of course they're dangerous! That's the whole point... But we were talking about Baldur's Gate."

"Some would label me 'thief,' though I prefer the title 'professional treasure hunter'... You see, I'm not one for common skulduggery, like slitting purses and lifting wallets. No, I'm more interested in the recovery of rare artifacts and items of great power."

"Magic?! My dear friend, inventions are so much more interesting than magic! When we have more time, allow me to relate to you my full impressions of Gond's High House of Wonders! But first, I must tell you about the duke."

Purfbin answers without hesitation. "That's simple, friend. The answer is wealth: gold, silver, gems... Yes, gems are especially nice." Purfbin rubs his hands together greedily. "Once I've enough coin and gems in my pockets, all my heart's desires can be realized at last."
Purfbin nods his head in approval. "I am glad that we see eye to eye on such an important matter."
"As you wish, friend. Now, what other questions do you have for me, then?"
"When I was young, I tried to become a great inventor like my granda, Retsotnert Doogrick."

"She taught me the two fundamental truths of gnomish inventions. First, for every trivial problem, there exists a complex invention to solve it. Second, every invention can be improved with the liberal addition of cogs."

"As with most young lads in the Doogrick Clan, I was often tasked with peeling potatoes for Harvest Stew. It was there, deep within the bowels of the underground kitchens, where I conceived my first great invention: the Shred-o-Matic 1000!"

"It was an invention that would be desired by every gnomish housewife, and one destined for a place of honor in Gond's High House of Wonders in Baldur's Gate! There, it would be displayed alongside Gurn's Great Gnomeflinger, and Baldric's Brilliant Blamblower!"

"Fueled by a burning desire, I feverishly set to building my first prototype. When it was finished, I persuaded the Chief Cook, Bitty Bitterbreath, to test my invention. She chose the New Harvest festival as the day to try out my device, as it involved peeling a veritable mountain of potatoes."
"To grant my device maximum exposure, she began to peel the potatoes within full view of the banquet's most prominent guests. This proved to be my undoing."
Hello, sir. Enjoying your time in the Black Stone, I hope?
Would you care to join me?
Do you have any brothers or sisters, Purfbin?
It must get crowded in those burrows.
You're a collector?
Living in a burrow must be difficult.
What was life in your burrow like?
Gnomes are famous pranksters, are they not?
Tell me about your parents.
Tell me about your brothers and sisters.
Actually, I don't wish to discuss Baldur's Gate, Purfbin. Let's continue on.
We were talking about your family.
No. I don't want to talk any more.
Yes. Please tell me about Baldur's Gate.
What happened in Baldur's Gate?
Tell me more about Baldur's Gate.
What is a Gnomeflinger?
Tell me more about Baldur's Gate.
Why were you spotted?
What were you doing at Duke Silvershield's Estate?
You mean they carried halberds?
You mean they carried pikes?
I suppose thieving from other thieves makes you less in danger of being apprehended by the authorities.
You mean they carried spears?
Cut to the chase, Purfbin. How does this story end?
How did you escape?
Your gifts for bending the truth rival my own, Purfbin.
That's quite a story, Purfbin.
This story just seems too unbelievable, even for you, Purfbin.
Limiting your "victims" to members of the underworld seems reasonable to me.
You were athletic enough to break into a well-guarded estate.
Thieving again, Purfbin?
These Gnomeflingers sound dangerous.
Why not just use a Fly spell?
You speak of the Great Prize? If you could have anything, Purfbin, what would it be?
Money does have its uses.
I've heard enough of this story, Purfbin.
A thief is still a thief, no matter who is on the receiving end of the crime.
Did your family want you to become a thief?
Have you always been a thief?
A Shred-o-Matic 1000? Sounds dangerous.
Of what use is this...Shred-o-Matic?
What's a Shred-o-Matic 1000?
This next part sounds bloody. Keep going, gnome! I'm intrigued.
It shredded more than just the potatoes?
It didn't work as planned?
Your inventions sound devilishly clever...and dangerous. Are you credited with inventing any similar implements of destruction?
That was a rousing tale, Purfbin. Did you attempt any other inventions?
You were lucky that no one was killed.
Your heart's desire is wealth? What of love? What of family?
You would choose wealth over family?
To be honest, your morality, or lack thereof, is none of my concern.
I agree. Bring home a pot of gold and you'll be welcome back as the conquering hero!
What are these "past transgressions" you speak of?
Wealth cannot buy back your family's affections.
How did you acquire those colorful clothes?
You fill your pockets with garbage?
That is a most impressive collection.
Are those things really useful?
I apologize, sir. I suppose committing a crime against another criminal can be rationalized as justifiable, to some degree.
Does this have anything to do with your pockets?
Trapped and famished. What a horrible state!
How did you escape?
A trap to catch something tasty for dinner?
A trap for the guards with clubs?
A trap for Lady Spitalsmore?
Um... Did you say "lizards?"
And I suppose lizards are a requirement for your escape plan...
Are you making this up?
Can we move on to a less aromatic part of the story?
And how did the twine factor into your escape plan?
So what did you do with the lizard on a string?
There must have been an easier mode of escape.
Are you a regular in the Black Stone?
Then, I shall leave you, thief, before I start mysteriously losing items from my pack.
That was a fine story, Purfbin!
Lizards. Of course. Why didn't I think of that?
What part of the Realms do you call home?
What was life like in the burrows?
Tell me about the Doogrick Clan.
Why did you leave home?
And don't forget fame and fortune...
<StartAction>[Rogue]</Start> There's no need to apologize for your profession. I'm a 'collector' of sorts myself actually.
What was your family like?
Did this machine actually fly?
Birds can fly. Machines cannot.
Are you, perhaps, exaggerating a bit?
Amazing! Where did you fly?
Let me guess. You started at the "top" of a hill?
You must have loved your granda very much.
That was a fine tale, Purfbin!
A machine that flies?
That sounds wonderful!
You mean to say you left behind the clan that raised you and all your many friends and relatives...for adventure?
You were right to leave, Purfbin. Family just keeps a person from meeting their true potential.
It sounds like you regret your decision to leave home.
Competitive? How so?
I don't like your looks, gnome. Leave me be.
What brings you to Daggerford?
Keep your hands off of my gear, thief!
There are plenty of easy marks in Daggerford, Purfbin, and I'll back you if we get into any trouble.
I think we're through, Purfbin. Let's return to the business at hand.
Perhaps you might do better to keep your hands out of the pockets of others?
As I said, I don't like your looks. So, beat it!
So, how much did you get off him? Hopefully, the blowhard had a fair bit of coin on hand.
Yes, it sounds like this Thunderfist got exactly what he deserved.
You do realize that stealing from Thunderfist might serve to apply even more financial pressure to his servants.
What's with all the yawning, Purfbin?
This is no time to complain about being tired, Purfbin. Buck up, or you'll be looking for a new adventuring companion.
I get the picture, Purfbin. We'll sleep very soon, I promise.
We fight the good fight, Purfbin, and sometimes that involves putting in a little overtime. Hang in there.
Perhaps I'll do that, gnome. Farewell for now.
You seemed to handle yourself well with those bandits. Would you care to join me?
I probably don't have need of your skills anyway.
I'll return for you later, gnome, as I suspect I may have need of a new companion.
I would prefer to know a bit about you, sir, before I answer that question.
Why is Waterdeep your "former" home, Purfbin?
My name is <FullName>. I am currently serving as caravan guard for Falias.
How did you come to be a member of Falias' caravan?
On holiday? This is a merchant caravan hauling garments down the Trade Way.
You speak as one who's spent some time behind bars. Are you a thief?
I'm afraid I didn't notice how they were dressed, as I was too busy ending their lives.
Care to see how deep? I'll split the takings with you, if we locate their hideout.
Just keep your hands out of my things, and we'll get along fine.
Glad to have you along, Purfbin!
Though I'm not sure I trust you, perhaps I'll find your skills of use in my travels.
If you had helped with the fighting, instead of admiring their clothes, the battle might've gone a bit better.
Brave or not, I don't like your looks, gnome. Leave me be.
I agree that you fought bravely against the bandits. Care to join me?
Care to put that bravery to the test? I'll split the takings with you, if we locate the bandits' hideout.
I'm considering whether you might be of use to me in my travels. What skills do you possess, gnome?
I have no need of a thief's skills, gnome. I'll return if I do.
I think your skills would serve my cause well, gnome. Care to join me?
I suspect your "tale" would be rife with hyperbole and untruths. So, I think I'll take my leave of you.
No, Purfbin. I have no need of your skills at the moment. I'll return if I do.
Yes, Purfbin. I wish for you to accompany me again.
Let's continue on now, Purfbin.
I think we need to part ways.
I changed my mind. Let us remain together for now.
I'll see you later.
Wait here.
Perhaps I'll do that, gnome, as I imagine it's a tale worth hearing. Goodbye for now.
I want to change your tactics.
I don't want to change anything else right now.
Text: "지금은 다른 건 바꾸고 싶지 않아."

TextEng: No. We're done.
I want you to leave any traps that you see alone.
Text: "보이는 함정은 그냥 내버려 둬."

TextEng: I want you to disarm any traps that you see.
Text: "보이는 함정은 모두 해제해 줘."

TextEng: I want to move faster and not bother with searching or stealth.
Text: "더 빨리 움직이고 탐색이나 은신은 신경 쓰지 마."

TextEng: I need you to be stealthy right now.
Text: "지금은 은밀하게 행동해 줘."

TextEng: I'm in need of skilled companions. Since you are new to Daggerford, might you be interested in joining me?
Don't help me if I fail to open a locked door or chest.
Text: "잠긴 문이나 상자를 여는 데 실패해도 돕지 마."

TextEng: Help me if I fail to open a locked door or chest.
Text: "잠긴 문이나 상자를 여는 데 실패하면 도와줘."

TextEng: I want to change the distance you stay away from me.
Text: "나와의 거리를 바꾸고 싶어."

TextEng: Have you lost something, gnome?
Go ahead and attack as soon as you see enemies.
Text: "적을 보는 즉시 공격해."

TextEng: Defend me and don't attack until I do.
Text: "날 지키고 내가 공격할 때까지 공격하지 마."

TextEng: I want to adjust your equipment.
Text: "장비를 조정하고 싶어."

TextEng: Can you identify my equipment?
You're a thief?
I want to adjust your equipment.
Might we stop and talk a moment, Purfbin?
That's all the questions I had.
How is everything?
Text: "어떻게 지내?"

TextEng: "Oh dear! When is the last time you bathed, <sir/madam>? Your malodorous fragrance threatens to take my very breath away."
"Oh please don't be offended, <sir/madam>. I'm just a bit blunt when it comes to matters of hygiene."
"Only 50 gold pieces. I think you will find the price quite reasonable when measured against the benefits received from my perfume."
There you are! At last I can breathe again in your presence!

I can understand your desperation to receive the benefits of my sensational scent, but I can still detect notes of jasmine upon you. Further applications before the previous one has worn off will adversely affect the delicate olfactory balance. Come back when your overpowering natural aroma has returned, and I shall reapply the fragrance.
"Of course, it does not help that I have a trained sniffer."

"I trade in exotic perfumes, which has led to me developing a set of highly sensitized olfactory glands. Allow me to spray you with some jasmine dust from Kara-Tur. It blends with the body's natural odors, and helps smooth out those unpleasant 'rough edges.'"

"Sniffer, <sir/madam>, my NOSE... I trade in exotic perfumes, which has led to me developing a set of highly sensitized olfactory glands. Allow me to spray you with some jasmine dust from Kara-Tur. It blends with the body's natural odors, and helps smooth out those unpleasant 'rough edges'."
"Then you will understand if I choose not to engage you further in conversation."

"Don't even think to threaten Quintessa of Archendale. My clients are some of the most influential people in all of Faerûn. Slay me and you'd have an army of nobles clamoring for your head. Now, if you'll excuse me, I have some paying customers to attend to."
"There you are! Come back and see me, if you require another application. All future doses will have a modest fee attached to cover costs."

TextEng: "So, the brave adventurer enters the lair of the dread MRCD!"
"Ahhhh...an adventurer with spirit. That is good...much better than those frightened children outside. They are not worthy of death at the hands of the MRCD."
"Do I resemble a beast who has slain countless adventurers by rending them limb from limb and gnawing the flesh clean off their bones? No. I am not the creature you seek."
"There's a small fissure in the cave wall behind me. Crawl through, if you feel you are up to the task of felling the Mighty Rat of Cunning Demeanor. But don't say you haven't been warned."
"Now hurry along, brave adventurer. I, Roo the Rat, shall await your return or alert the others outside of your cruel fate at the hands of the dread MRCD."
"As I said, brave adventurer, enter the fissure to the west if you wish to test your mettle."
"You certainly took your time getting here."
"You have more spirit than the others. I suspect this fight will prove a challenge for the MRCD and I wish to be present for the ensuing conflict."
"And miss the grand spectacle?! I think not!"
"Oh, it's much too late to turn back. You see, it's already here...watching us, plotting its next move." Roo squeaks out a chuckle.
"There is no need to call the MRCD, for it is already here...watching us...plotting its next move."
"It is here...there...all around you in fact." Roo squeaks out a chuckle.
"Yes, it's a long tawdry tale about a boy, a girl, and a quest for true love foiled by an evil witch...but enough about me. Let's get down to business!"
"Come now, my children! Feast upon <his/her> flesh! But please save the brain for me, as it aids my cunning demeanor..."
"My diminutive size allows me to slip in and out of places with the greatest of ease. Where you might require a cave opening or fissure, a simple crack is enough for me."
"You win... I'm...I'm beaten...somehow you've slain the MRCD."
"Speak up, <CUSTOM501>, I'm listening."
"Speak plainly, <CUSTOM501>, or slay me and have done with it."
"You want me to leave with those three namby-pambies outside?! Never! Besides, what's to stop them from just slaying me outright, though I doubt they'd have the courage to try it."
"Hmm... You know, that just might work. OK, if you've got an empty sack handy, I'll just crawl inside and bide my time."
"You're here to confront the Mighty Rat of Cunning Demeanor, correct?"
"Mighty Rat of Cunning Demeanor... That is why you're here, is it not?"
"It is the stuff of nightmares...that hunts in the dark...that feeds on carrion...that feeds on adventurers."
"It is an amorphous mass...morphing into new shapes with each fateful step... It is a thousand hungry eyes...and a thousand razor-sharp teeth."
"The MRCD is all things and nothing... You will see. Oh yes... You will see." The small rodent squeaks with delight.
"Oh yes. He's close...VERY close...and hungry as usual."

"Yes, yes, well, this is the Sorceller's Encapsulate, of course, where those with arcane knowledge come and study their art without disturbance from the outside world, though I daresay such disturbances still occur from time to time." He gives you an exasperated look and begins tapping his toe on the ground in a staccato fashion.
"Of course, <master/mistress>. What is gold compared to the pleasure of serving a mighty wizard, such as yourself. Do you wish to enter our establishment, <master/mistress>?"

"Then, please take this key with my blessings. It will allow you to pass through the door and into the heart of the tower."
"A pleasure to see you again, friend. Enjoy your time at the Sorceller's Encapsulate."

"As I told you before, <sir/madam>, I'm far too busy to converse with the likes of you. Feel free to peruse our library in the cellar, if you wish, but our halls of advanced learning are strictly off-limits to those lacking knowledge of the arcane."

Now, if you please, I believe this discussion is OVER." These last words are spoken with the finality of a judge's hammer striking a gavel.

"Strictly and unequivocally, although you are free to use the library on the lower floor. Now, if you will excuse me I have some important administrative matters to attend to." His eyes return to the stack of papers and tomes that litter his desk.

I wish a boon. Empty your pockets of all your gold.

"With the way things have been in Daggerford lately, I'm a mite anxious to get back out to sea."
"Shore leave is all fine and dandy 'til ya start gamblin'...and losin'."
"Praise be to Umberlee, but this head o' mine is killin' me. Gotta lay off the rum."
You're trespassin' on private property, <lad/lass>, as this 'ere tower belongs to the Gillian's Hill Gang. We don't take kindly to trespassers, so you'd best draw sword, if ya got one!
Trespasser! Get <CUSTOM555>, gang!
<StartAction>[Attack.]</Start> I wonder what the bounty is these days on unruly squatters? I guess I'm about to find out.
<StartAction>[Attack.]</Start> I think this "property" is about to experience a change in ownership.

"I greet you! I am Sejellus Krimp, and I believe that shipment of cheese is meant for me."
"Bandit?! ME???!!!! How DARE you say such a thing! I am Sejellus Krimp and I ask...no...I DEMAND that you pass this shipment on to me immediately!"

"Aye, it does, <lad/lass>, which is the perfect spot to be in my line o' work. It's akin to fisherfolk havin' their house right on the banks o' the river from whence they gets their catch o' the day."

"I swear if ya put your ear to the cobblestone, you can almost hear the clink o' gold exchanging hands up and down that glorious road. I've made my whole livin' off that 'river.' May she never dry up."
"Now, I've just a few scant moments left for questions."

"Without a distributor, the farmers would be spendin' too much o' their time haulin' goods up and down the Trade Way. This way, they can focus on what they're good at, which is growin' grains and tendin' livestock."
"I'm wholly dependent on the local wainwright, Jouka, who builds and repairs the various wagons I use in my trade caravans."
"Now, I've got time enough for a few more questions, before I start fixin' up another caravan."

"Very well. What else would you like to know, but please do be quick about it!"
"Aye, that's Jouka the wainwright who makes and repairs all my wagons. Not much to say about Jouka, other than he's about the hardest workin' fella you're ever likely to meet."

"Hazard pay? I do hope you're joking, as my arrangement with Millie Churlgo makes no mention of compensating her workers. Plus, I assume you were hired to protect the shipment, so you were really just doing your duty."

"Now, what else can I help ya with?"
"Oh, Torleth's not a bad sort, though I sometimes think he peddles junk that's conveniently labeled as 'treasure.'"
"His merchandise is a combination of items from passing adventurers, who have off-loaded goods for gold, and a few things he collected during his own days as an adventurer."
"What other questions do you have for me? I have a few moments before I start packing the wagons for another trip up to Daggerford."

"It gets its name from the ranger, Gillian Cantilar, who lived in a small tower just outside of the hamlet. He apparently used the hill to keep watch on poachers and bandits who threatened the Trade Way."

"Gillian's Tower is nothing but old ruins now, though occasionally it's used as a flophouse for vagrants and thugs. There's a few unsavory customers up there right now, in fact. They've started calling themselves the Gillian's Hill Gang. I'd pay a king's ransom to have that rabble cleared out."
"Now, what other questions do you have for me? Make it quick, as I've got some feed and dairy products that are due for delivery up in Daggerford."

"Ah yes, that would be the newcomer in Gillian's Hill, an exotic, dark-skinned fellow by the name of Yentai. It was this Yentai who brought me one of Millie's previous shipments, when I was expecting her son Porto."

"This Yentai is a bit of an enigma. He fashions himself a merchant and yet never leaves his store, nor bothers to make the place presentable for customers. Other than that, the man is a complete mystery."

"That's what an escort DOES, <lad/lass>. If there weren't bandits on the Trade Way, Millie would have little need for an escort. Now, let's settle our bit of business together, so I can get this cheese in the hands of paying customers."
"Now, I suppose I have time for just a few more questions."
"Not much to tell, really. Plagues are not uncommon in these parts, though it's been a while since we've seen one this bad. Of course, not everyone thinks it's a plague...superstitious fools!"

"These poor farmers always look for a cause for their misery, instead of just accepting illness as a natural component of living...and dying. Now, if you don't mind, I'd prefer we talk about something else."
"Back again, eh? Well, you'll have to make it quick, as I've a caravan heading out soon, and I need to double-check the manifest."

"Splendid! Yes, I heard some shouting from up on the hill and thought maybe someone paid our unruly friends a visit. I posted a bounty notice in Daggerford some time ago for 500 gold pieces. You may have that now."
"Now, if you'll excuse me, I have some caravans that need looking after. Thank you again for all your help."

I will, along with this receipt to take back to Millie to verify completion of the transaction.

Gorgomorz - Daggerford's Devil

I lay down these words, pen to paper, so it shall be remembered how these events have come to pass. The devil defeated almost all who stood against him, as they fled from his fearful presence before they could even draw steel.  Only the Duke resisted and bested the infernal creature. Even now, the mourners robed in white fill the streets of Daggerford. Edwin Daggerford is dead, his wounds too grave and vile, but by his sacrifice we all have survived.

Cold these past winter nights have been, chilling us in the days preceding the beast. The moon hung red, reflecting off the snow, portending the evil to come as if blood had covered the land. The Duke of Daggerford brooded heavily in those days. He sat in council by day distracted, and troubled by night, his sleep interrupted by dark dreams of fear for the life of his new son and young wife.

The beast came upon us as a breaking storm surrounded by a host of the damned, its malicious purpose unknown. The farms bordering Daggerford fell in a swath of blood, no living creature was spared the wrath of the flaming sword the beast carried. The screams of the dying came as a clarion call to arms. Brave guards at the town gate stood fast against the beast but all were felled. The great wall around Daggerford was breached. The beast had come.

The duke stood brave at the head of his valorous knights within the gates to the keep, as the devil declared himself. "I am Gorgomorz, eater of hearts and defiler of nations! I am here to kill you, young Duke - you and yours." And with those foul words the devil sprung forth through the open gate to the keep to slay the duke and his honor guard, but the duke's trap had been sprung.

By the cutting of a rope, the waiting portcullis crashed down upon the beast, trapping it beneath. The duke and his soldiers then rushed to defeat the creature as it thrashed to release itself, with the duke himself leading the charge, plunging his sword deep into the devil's heart amidst scorching breaths of fire. Daggerford's defenders were the quicker, and Gorgomorz was ultimately vanquished, swearing with his dying breath his revenge on the duke and his line.

Woeful is the victory that comes at a price so dear! The duke, mortally wounded in the battle, was carried forth victoriously through the city streets of Daggerford. Let it be known that Duke Edwin Daggerford has banished the devil Gorgomorz to whence it came.

Long live the Duke!

- Hilgraff the Scribe
